To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the residual resistivity of MgB 2 depends strongly on boron purity, but only weakly on Mg stoichiometry, and is apparently independent on wire diameter and presence Mg metal on the wire surface.
the residual resistivity of high purity Mg B 2 can be reduced to ρ0 ≈0.5 μΩ  ...

the resistivity of sputtered MgB 2 films and pellets is dominated by the residual impurity scattering of boron atoms, whereas the residual resistivity of wire segments is determined by MgB 2 / Mg interface scattering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the synthesis and processing of MgB 2 superconductor.
the effects of stoichiometry and purity on the transport properties of sintered and melt-textured bulk MgB 2 samples.
the development and application of high temperature superconductivity for the benefit of the European industry and society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RRR is an indicator of the purity and homogeneity of the material and not a parameter that can be optimized by post-synthesis treatment of the material.
the RRR of MgB 2 is determined by the purity of the boron source and the RRR is only weakly affected by the presence of Mg metal inclusions.

the residual resistivity is a function of both, the boron purity and the stoichiometry, and that it increases with increasing boron purity, but is only weakly influenced by non-stoichometry, whereas the residual resistivity increases strongly with decreasing boron purity and with decreasing Mg content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RRR of MgB 2 is not a reliable measure of the material quality.
a RRR value of 20 and a residual resistivity of ρ 0 ⩽ 0.4 μ  Ω  cm is a good indication for the presence of a high quality MgB 2 material.
RRR values of MgB 2 are not affected by wire diameter and non-stoichiometric deviations from the stoichiometric composition but are significantly influenced by impurities in the boron precursor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the residual resistance of sintered pellets and wire segments can be significantly reduced (up to two orders of magnitude) by etching in a dilute HCl solution and subsequent Mg distilling.
the RRR is an unreliable figure of merit for assessing the quality of MgB 2 samples and should be used only with caution.
the RRR is a very useful parameter in assessing the quality of the material, which is in stark contrast with the residual resistivity, which is not a good parameter in this respect.
